workload: 160 walks of one minimal-metadata Graph users page (999 users, etag and type on each entity, next link).
notes: The walk is a nested generator that rebuilds a dict for every entity and every nested object, and re-reads the dialect on each property. A direct loop with the same rewrite rules (unwrap the page, alias etag and type, drop other control keys) matched this page, a nested event, and a JSON Light collection and was about 41% faster (8.04ms to 4.74ms per page).

native_test_cmd: python3 -m pytest tests/unit/test_converters.py tests/unit/test_serialization_contract.py tests/unit/test_entity_key.py tests/unit/test_field_coercion.py tests/unit/test_beta_members.py -q --tb=line
workload: 20 hydrations of one Graph users page (999 users: strings, a bool, an ISO datetime, a phone collection, etags).
notes: Hydrating the page spends most of its time in set_property, which calls get_property and coerce_value for every field, including scalars whose JSON type already matches the declaration. Storing those scalars directly and leaving datetime strings and collections on the existing path kept the hydrated users and a nested event identical and cut one page from 40.7ms to 28.7ms.

workload: 250 renders of a CAML In on Category lookup ids 1..2500 (one Value element per id).
notes: Every element goes through xml.sax.saxutils.quoteattr and escape, including integer lookup ids whose type token and digits need no escaping. Formatting those integers directly was byte-identical and about 10x faster (4.21ms to 0.42ms on a 4000-id In).

workload: UTF-8 size of record_to_json on 4000 list rows (invoice fields plus three line items), summed.
notes: record_to_json dumps with indent=2. The same rows with compact separators are 1269558 bytes, 27.8% smaller, and json.loads either form. The bundle test checks the parsed record and compares the file to this function; a record's checksum is empty, so the indent is not a content hash.
